text:
mariana: hey team — hitting a weird regression after converting a SentencePiece HF checkpoint to Redwood BPE for chat bring-up. few-shot examples in the chat template are getting mangled, and generated completions insert extra spaces or split tokens mid-word.

olivia: can you paste a minimal repro tokenization for the same string with both tokenizers? spm vs converted-bpe.

mariana: sure, here's a short diagnostic I ran locally (huggingface):

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
spm = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('hf/locale-spm-small', use_fast=False)
# this is the converted tokenizer we will push to Redwood
bpe = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local/converted-bpe', use_fast=False)
print('spm ids:', spm.encode('User: Hello there'))
print('bpe ids :', bpe.encode('User: Hello there'))
print('spm toks:', spm.convert_ids_to_tokens(spm.encode('User: Hello there')))
print('bpe toks :', bpe.convert_ids_to_tokens(bpe.encode('User: Hello there')))
```

mariana: results: spm encodes "User:" as [345, 12, ...] and tokens ['▁User', ':'] but converted-bpe gives [345, 12, ...] too *but* token strings differ and some subwords map to same id as special tokens — looks like an id collision after remapping.

kai: ugh id collisions. we saw this before when the conversion script reuses ids instead of appending new vocab entries. did you preserve special_tokens_map and ensure reserved ids aren't overwritten?

sam: quick checklist: 1) confirm vocab size matches in config.json (vocab_size vs actual vocab file lines). 2) check special_tokens_map in tokenizer config. 3) run an encode->decode roundtrip: decode(encode(s)) == s (or close).

mariana: config.json in the converted bundle had "vocab_size": 50256 but the vocab file had 50254 lines. two tokens dropped and their ids got reassigned, which probably caused the collision with <pad>/<eos>.

olivia: that mismatch is a red flag. also some conversion tools collapse identical strings into single entries but don't update merges/ids consistently. In chat templates that use explicit separators like "</s>\nUser:", that can change the token boundaries and break few-shot prompting.

kai: are you using sentencepiece's model to export raw token strings before conversion? recommended flow: export spm vocab -> canonicalize unicode -> keep special tokens at the end and reserve N ids -> then generate merges if moving to BPE. If you generate BPE merges but keep old ids, you get ordering problems.

mariana: good point. I used tokenizers-cli convert which tried to be smart but apparently didn't respect reserved ids. I'll try a manual export: `spm_export_vocab --model spm.model > spm_vocab.txt` then build the bpe vocab from that, preserving special tokens at the tail.

sam: also add a CI test for tokenizer parity: sample 200 prompt strings from our eval set, verify top-1 token from spm encode equals top-1 token from converted encode after id remap table. fail the job if mismatch > 0.5%.

eval-bot: quick-run: small parity check on 200 examples -> 7 mismatches (3.5%). Most mismatches are around punctuation and the 'User:' marker. See /tmp/tokenizer-parity-1764123456.log

olivia: 3.5% is definitely enough to cause prompt-template fragility. Two actionable fixes: 1) rebuild conversion pipeline to keep id mapping explicit and append any new tokens; 2) ensure config.json vocab_size matches and include a token id remap table in the bundle so Redwood import can detect collisions.

mariana: I'll try option (1) first — re-export and rebuild using a script that produces a map old_id->new_id and a small metadata file. pinging @olivia for review once I have a patch.

olivia: happy to review. also include a small unit test that asserts special token ids are > vocab_size-50 (we reserve last 50 ids for specials in our convention).

kai: FYI when converting for chat templates, canonicalize whitespace tokens: spm uses '▁' to indicate spaces which BPE often represents as explicit tokens. We have a small helper in infra/convert_tokenizers that normalizes these differences — consider running that.

mariana: noted, will run normalizer + rebuild. thanks all.

sam: glad we caught this before dedicated rollout. mark as P1 for the onboarding tracker?

mariana: marking P1 and adding blockers to the PR. thanks :thumbsup:
